name: Mountain Pose
description: A foundational standing pose promoting alignment and grounding.
precaution: Avoid locking your knees; keep a gentle micro-bend.
steps: Stand with your feet either hip-width apart or together, ensuring all four corners of each foot press evenly into the ground.
Spread your toes wide and gently lift your arches while rooting down through your heels.
Engage the thigh muscles slightly as you stack your knees directly over your ankles.
Lengthen through the legs and draw your belly gently inward to support the spine.
Roll shoulders up, back, and down, letting shoulder blades soften down the back.
Lift the crown of your head toward the sky, keeping chin parallel to the floor.
Relax your face and jaw while maintaining steady breath.
quote: “In the stillness of the mountain, you find the foundation of all movement.”

name: Downward-Facing Dog
description: An essential inverted pose forming a strong V-shape.
benefit: Stretches spine, hamstrings, shoulders, and strengthens arms.
precaution: Bend knees if hamstrings are tight; avoid wrist strain.
steps: Begin on hands and knees with wrists directly under shoulders and knees beneath hips.
Spread your fingers wide and root through the knuckles of your hands to protect the wrists.
Curl your toes under and lift your knees off the ground as you raise your hips upward.
Gradually begin to straighten your legs without locking the knees; keep heels moving toward the floor.
Lengthen your spine by pressing your chest gently toward your thighs.
Relax your head and neck, letting ears align with biceps.
Engage your core and breathe deeply, keeping weight evenly distributed between hands and feet.
quote: “Root down through the hands to rise through the hips.”

name: Child’s Pose
description: A gentle resting pose that relaxes the spine and hips.
benefit: Calms the nervous system and releases back tension.
precaution: Avoid if experiencing severe knee injury.
steps: Begin on your hands and knees, bringing your big toes together.
Separate your knees as wide as comfortable, allowing hips to sink back toward your heels.
Walk your hands forward as you fold your torso down between or over your thighs.
Rest your forehead on the mat, a block, or stacked hands.
Extend arms forward for an active stretch or bring them alongside your legs for a more restorative variation.
Soften shoulders, jaw, and belly while lengthening through the spine.
Breathe slowly, allowing each exhale to deepen your sense of rest.

name: Cobra Pose
description: A gentle backbend lifting the chest up from the ground.
precaution: Avoid compressing lower back; use gentle lift.
steps: Lie flat on your stomach with the tops of your feet pressing into the mat.
Place your hands under your shoulders, elbows hugging close to your ribcage.
Press lightly into your palms as you begin lifting your head and chest.
Engage your back muscles rather than pushing heavily with your hands.
Keep elbows slightly bent and shoulders relaxed away from ears.
Lift only as high as feels comfortable without compressing the lower back.
Keep your gaze forward or slightly upward while maintaining smooth breath.
quote: “Rise with the heart of a cobra—steady, open, awake.”

name: Upward-Facing Dog
description: A deeper backbend supported by hands and feet.
benefit: Opens chest, strengthens arms and wrists.
precaution: Avoid if experiencing lower-back pain.
steps: Lie on your belly with legs extended behind you and tops of feet pressing into the mat.
Place your palms beside your lower ribs, elbows pointing backward.
Press into your hands as you lift your chest, straightening your arms.
Activate your quadriceps to lift your thighs and pelvis off the mat.
Roll shoulders back and lift through the sternum, expanding the chest.
Keep the back of your neck long and gaze slightly forward.
Engage your core to avoid collapsing into the lower back.
quote: “Lift the heart and let the breath guide your expansion.”

name: Plank Pose
description: A strength-building pose like the top of a pushup.
benefit: Strengthens core, arms, and stabilizing muscles.
precaution: Avoid letting hips sag; maintain alignment.
steps: Begin on your hands and knees and step your feet back one at a time.
Press firmly into your palms, keeping shoulders stacked over wrists.
Straighten your legs and engage your thighs, drawing energy up the legs.
Engage the core by drawing the belly inward toward the spine.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Press your heels back while lengthening forward through the crown of your head.
Maintain steady breath while avoiding sinking hips or bowing the back.

name: Chaturanga
description: A low pushup strengthening the upper body.
benefit: Builds arm, shoulder, and core strength.
precaution: Avoid if you have shoulder issues.
steps: Begin in Plank Pose with shoulders aligned over wrists.
Shift your body slightly forward so shoulders pass your wrists.
Bend elbows straight back, keeping them hugging the ribcage.
Lower your torso in a straight line without dropping the hips.
Stop when elbows reach a 90-degree angle, maintaining control.
Engage your core and legs to keep the body stable.
Hold briefly before transitioning to Upward-Facing Dog or lowering fully to the floor.
quote: “Control the descent; honor the strength within.”

name: Warrior I
description: A powerful lunge with square hips and lifted arms.
precaution: Keep the front knee aligned with toes.
steps: Step one foot forward into a deep lunge with the front knee stacked over the ankle.
Turn the back heel down at a 45-degree angle, pressing firmly into the outer edge of the foot.
Square your hips forward by gently drawing the back hip toward the front.
Raise your arms overhead with palms facing each other.
Lengthen through your spine while rooting down through both feet.
Relax shoulders away from ears as you lift through the chest.
Keep breath steady while maintaining front-knee alignment.
quote: “Stand tall like a warrior—focused and rooted.”

name: Warrior II
description: A wide stance pose with arms extended horizontally.
precaution: Avoid letting the front knee collapse inward.
steps: From a standing position, step your feet wide apart—about a leg-length distance.
Turn your right foot out 90 degrees and your left foot slightly inward.
Align your front heel with the arch of your back foot.
Bend your front knee to 90 degrees, ensuring the knee tracks over the second and third toes.
Extend your arms out to shoulder height, parallel to the floor.
Relax your shoulders and reach equally through both fingertips.
Keep your torso upright as you gaze over your front hand.
Press into the outer edge of your back foot to maintain stability.
quote: “Where your gaze goes, your energy flows.”

name: Warrior III
description: A balancing pose with torso and leg extending parallel to the floor.
benefit: Builds balance, focus, and leg strength.
precaution: Use wall support if necessary.
steps: Begin in a lunge with your front knee bent and back leg extended.
Shift weight into your front foot as you lean your torso forward.
Simultaneously lift your back leg off the ground, extending it straight behind you.
Create a long line from the crown of your head through your lifted heel.
Keep hips level by dropping the outer hip of the lifted leg slightly.
Extend your arms forward, back, or out to the sides for balance.
Engage your core and keep your standing leg strong.
Maintain steady breath as you hold your balance.

name: Triangle Pose
description: A standing side-body stretch with extended arms.
benefit: Improves flexibility in spine and hips.
precaution: Avoid hyperextending knees.
steps: Stand with your feet wide apart, about a leg-length distance.
Turn your right foot out 90 degrees and left foot slightly inward.
Extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Reach your right arm forward while keeping both sides of the waist long.
Hinge at the hip and tilt your torso over your right leg.
Place your right hand on your shin, block, or the floor—depending on flexibility.
Extend your left arm straight upward, stacking shoulders vertically.
Gaze upward or keep the neck neutral based on comfort.

name: Extended Side Angle
description: A deep lunge with side-body lengthening.
precaution: Keep spine long; avoid collapsing.
steps: Begin in Warrior II with your front knee bent at 90 degrees.
Bring your front elbow to rest gently on your thigh or place your hand on a block or floor.
Extend your top arm overhead, creating a diagonal line from foot to fingertips.
Rotate your chest upward, avoiding collapsing forward.
Press into the outer edge of your back foot for stability.
Draw your lower ribs in to keep the spine long.
Engage the core and breathe steadily as you deepen the stretch.

name: Reverse Warrior
description: A heart-opening side bend from Warrior II.
benefit: Stretches side waist and strengthens legs.
precaution: Avoid overextension in lower back.
steps: Start in Warrior II with your front knee bent and arms extended.
Flip your front palm upward and reach that arm overhead.
Slide your back hand down your back leg without collapsing weight onto it.
Lift your chest as you lengthen through your side body.
Keep the front knee deeply bent and aligned over the toes.
Avoid dumping into the lower back by engaging the core.
Gaze upward or forward depending on neck comfort.
quote: “Move like a wave — strong yet fluid.”

name: Chair Pose
description: A dynamic standing squat that strengthens lower body.
benefit: Builds power in legs and core.
precaution: Avoid overarching lower back.
steps: Stand with your feet together or hip-width apart.
Bend your knees and sit your hips back as if lowering into a chair.
Keep your knees aligned with your toes and weight in your heels.
Lift your arms overhead, palms facing inward.
Draw your tailbone down slightly to avoid overarching your lower back.
Lengthen through the spine and lift the chest.
Engage your core and breathe deeply as you hold the posture.

name: Tree Pose
description: A one-legged standing balance pose.
precaution: Avoid placing foot on knee joint.
steps: Begin standing in Mountain Pose with arms at your sides.
Shift your weight into your left foot, grounding firmly.
Lift your right foot and place the sole on your left ankle, calf, or inner thigh—avoiding the knee.
Press foot and leg together to create stability.
Bring hands to heart center or raise them overhead.
Keep your gaze steady on a fixed point to improve balance.
Engage your core and maintain slow, deep breathing.

name: Bridge Pose
description: A gentle backbend lifting the hips upward.
precaution: Avoid turning your head while in the pose.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet hip-width apart.
Walk your feet close to your hips with toes pointing forward.
Press firmly into your feet as you lift your hips upward.
Roll your shoulders under and interlace your fingers beneath your body if comfortable.
Lift your chest toward your chin without compressing the neck.
Engage glutes and thighs to support the lift.
Breathe smoothly, keeping the neck neutral.
quote: “Lift your heart and let it open.”

name: Seated Forward Fold
description: A deep seated stretch for hamstrings and spine.
benefit: Calms the mind and lengthens the back body.
precaution: Keep the spine long; avoid rounding excessively.
steps: Sit tall on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Adjust your sitting bones by gently rocking side to side to find a grounded base.
Flex your feet so your toes point upward, engaging the legs.
Inhale and lengthen your spine, reaching your arms overhead.
Hinge forward from your hips as you exhale, keeping the spine long.
Reach your hands to your shins, ankles, or feet—wherever is accessible without strain.
Relax your neck and soften your shoulders while maintaining gentle length in the spine.
Breathe deeply, allowing each exhale to help you soften into the stretch.
quote: “Fold not in force, but in surrender.”

name: Boat Pose
description: A core-strengthening balance on the sit bones.
precaution: Avoid collapsing chest or rounding the back.
steps: Begin seated with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Sit tall and lean back slightly while keeping the spine long.
Lift your feet off the ground, bringing shins parallel to the floor.
Engage your core and balance on your sit bones.
Extend your arms forward at shoulder height with palms facing each other.
For a deeper variation, straighten your legs to form a V-shape with your body.
Keep your chest lifted and breath steady as you hold.

name: Camel Pose
description: A deep backbend opening chest and front body.
precaution: Avoid dropping head too far back.
steps: Kneel on the floor with your knees hip-width apart and thighs perpendicular to the ground.
Place your hands on your lower back with fingers pointing down for support.
Lift your chest upward as you draw shoulder blades together.
Gently begin to arch your back, pressing hips forward.
If comfortable, reach your hands back one at a time to hold your heels.
Keep your neck neutral or allow a slight backward gaze without collapsing.
Engage your core and thighs as you breathe deeply in the posture.

name: Cat Cow Pose
description: A flowing spinal warm-up between arching and rounding.
precaution: Move slowly through transitions.
steps: Begin on your hands and knees in a tabletop position with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
For Cow Pose, inhale as you drop your belly, lift your chest, and tilt your pelvis upward.
Draw your shoulder blades back and lift your gaze slightly forward.
For Cat Pose, exhale as you round your spine upward, tucking chin and tailbone.
Press firmly into your palms and broaden your shoulder blades.
Flow smoothly between the two poses, matching movement with breath.
Maintain steady rhythm, allowing the spine to warm and loosen.

name: Half Lord of the Fishes
description: A seated spinal twist improving rotation.
precaution: Avoid deep twist if pregnant.
steps: Sit with your legs extended in front of you.
Bend your right knee and place your right foot outside your left thigh.
Bend your left leg and tuck the heel near your right hip if comfortable.
Lengthen your spine on an inhale, sitting tall.
Twist your torso toward your right knee as you exhale.
Place your left elbow outside your right knee and your right hand behind you for support.
Maintain length through your spine as you deepen the twist with each breath.
quote: “Twist to rinse the old and invite the new.”

name: Pigeon Pose
description: A deep hip opener targeting glutes and hip flexors.
benefit: Releases stored tension in the hips.
precaution: Support hips with blocks if needed.
steps: Begin in Downward-Facing Dog and lift your right leg upward.
Bring your right knee toward your right wrist while lowering your shin to the mat.
Extend your left leg straight behind you with the top of the foot resting on the floor.
Square your hips forward by drawing your right hip back and left hip forward.
Stay upright or walk your hands forward to fold over the front leg.
Rest your forehead on the mat or a prop as you relax into the stretch.
Breathe deeply, softening into the hips with each exhale.

name: Crow Pose
description: An arm balance requiring focus and core strength.
precaution: Practice with a soft surface if new.
steps: Begin in a low squat with feet hip-width apart and hands shoulder-width in front of you.
Spread your fingers wide and press firmly into the mat.
Lift your hips and place your knees high on your upper arms or triceps.
Shift your weight forward gradually, keeping gaze ahead—not down.
Engage your core as you lean forward further onto your hands.
Lift one foot at a time, eventually raising both to balance fully.
Keep breath steady and arms strong without locking elbows.

name: Happy Baby
description: A gentle hip opener lying on the back.
precaution: Avoid rocking too aggressively.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent toward your chest.
Grab the outer edges of your feet with your hands.
Open your knees wider than your torso, keeping ankles over knees.
Flex your feet and gently pull them downward to deepen the stretch.
Keep your lower back grounded on the mat.
Optionally rock side to side to massage the spine.
Relax your jaw, shoulders, and breath.
